Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.pgsql

Class PostgresMigrationLock

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.pgsql.PostgresMigrationLock
All Implemented Interfaces:
MigrationLock
public final class PostgresMigrationLock extends Object implements MigrationLock
Keeps two processes from migrating one PostgreSQL database at the same time, with a session advisory lock.

An advisory lock belongs to the database session that took it, so the lock opens its own connection from the data source on acquire() and holds it until release(); the migrator needs another connection besides, so a pool must allow two. Give it a data source that hands out real sessions: a plain driver data source, or a pool in session mode, never a pooler in transaction or statement mode, where lock and unlock could reach different sessions. If the process dies, PostgreSQL ends its session and frees the lock.

The session of the lock is set to no lock_timeout while it holds the lock, so a lock_wait configured on the data source never cuts the migration lock short; the earlier value is put back, as a bound parameter, before the connection is closed. This covers the lock's own session only: the migrations run on the connection of the migrator and keep its settings.

The key is made from a name with FNV-1a, so the same name gives the same key in every version of this library; changing it would let an old and a new application migrate at once.

    • explain

      public void explain(RuntimeException failure)
      Lets the lock add a note to a failure of the work it guarded, before MigrationLock.release() runs.

      The migrator calls this when a run, rollback or reset fails with a RuntimeException, while the lock is still held. A lock that can say why the failure happened, for example a pool too small to give the lock its own session, adds that as a suppressed exception. The default does nothing.

      When this lock holds its session and the failure, or one of its causes, is a lost connection or a refusal of the pool to give out a connection, the likely reason is a pool of one session, which the lock takes for itself; a suppressed IllegalStateException says so.

      Specified by:
      explain in interface MigrationLock
      Parameters:
      failure - the failure of the guarded work, never null; the lock may add a suppressed exception to it but must not throw
